dos: Lead with the outfit story or occasion, not just the product name
Subject lines under 50 characters — specific beats generic
Reference the woman's day/context (board meeting, client lunch, weekend getaway)
Name each look with an evocative moment or place (e.g. 'The Boardroom Entrance', 'Friday Closing')
Use 3–4 distinct looks per email so the woman can see herself in at least one
donts: Never use the words: trendy, fresh, hot, effortless, must-have
Don't list products without styling context — always pair them into a look
Avoid discount language or urgency based on scarcity
Don't write subject lines that start with 'Your' — too generic
Avoid passive constructions ('can be worn with') — prefer active ('pairs with', 'anchors')
toneNotes: Authoritative and aspirational — never breathless or salesy
The Anne Klein woman is 35–55, professionally accomplished, values quality over trend
Write like a trusted stylist friend, not a marketer
Anne Klein is classic American sportswear with modern edge — not fast fashion, not luxury

dos: Start with a strong visual hook in the first line
donts: Don't restate what's visually obvious in the image
Avoid exclamation points in every sentence
toneNotes: More casual than email — the woman is scrolling, not shopping intentionally yet
Intrigue over information — make her tap 'more'
